messages:
sam: Heads-up, ap-southeast-1 GPU pools are showing a steady increase in pod evictions (OOM/killed) over the last 6m. GSLB started steering ~18% traffic to eu-west as health scores dropped. Autoscaler isn't converging.

maria: Seeing the same in the console. Pod restarts + one host flapping out of the pool. Any recent image or runtime changes?

aj: No deploys in region in last 24h. Looks like disk pressure + kernel OOM on a subset of nodes (from node logs). Could be a driver/kernel regression on that host class.

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-node-group-ap-southeast-1 - 7/48 nodes NotReady; evictions rate 12/min; avg pod restart 3.2.

liam: We should soft-drain overloaded AZs and shift traffic gradually — keep affinity for warm KV caches. Full shift will blow cold-cache latency. Propose GSLB weight change: ap-southeast-1 -> 60%, eu-west -> 25%, na-west -> 15% with 5m TTL.

nora: Cost flag: shifting to na-west increases egress and cross-region infra cost. We need an override if customer SLAs require low latency. Otherwise prefer eu-west.

sam: Agreed. For now do a gradual 15% per 3m step until evictions drop under 1/min or CPU mem pressure clears. Can we do a canary to a subset of routes (model-large vs model-small)?

aj: Yes — runbook suggests routing by model tag. We'll keep model-large at 30% max to eu-west to avoid overloading EU pools. Also enabling prefix KV cache passthrough on eu-west to reduce cold penalty.

maria: If we change GSLB weights, include a short TTL and set failover policy to fallback only after 2 consecutive health checks fail. We don't want flip-flopping.

liam: I'll apply a staged update via the GSLB API. Command I'll run: 
```json
POST /v1/gslb/policy/update
{ "policy_id": "global-default", "overrides": { "ap-southeast-1": 60, "eu-west": 25, "na-west": 15 }, "step_secs": 180, "min_ttl": 300 }
```

sam: Also open a CAC ticket to spin up replacement node hosts in ap-southeast-1 if host failures keep rising. If it's a driver regression, we may need to pin the runtime to last-known-good image.

infra-bot: DEPLOYMENT_HOOK: gslb/rolling-update started by liam (1748503320).

aj: After first step (15% shift), monitor 10-20 p999 latency for the model-large endpoints and pod eviction rate. If p999 increases >200ms in eu-west, pause.

maria: I'll message product/success with the mitigation plan and ETA. cc @ops-oncall for extra eyeballs.

liam: Update: first step done at 1748503340, ap-southeast-1 -> 85% -> 70%? (weights take effect over TTL). Watching metrics.

sam: Thanks. If we need faster relief we can temporarily override the cost-based routing rule (cost-penalty: na-west) — but confirm budget owner.

nora: Budget owner pinged; they've pre-approved emergency override up to $8k/day for this region incident. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:

aj: Noting follow-up actions: 1) run node health harvest + collect dmesg from failed hosts; 2) prepare kernel-driver rollback; 3) optional repro on staging.

infra-bot: ALERT: eviction rate in ap-southeast-1 dropped to 4/min after step 2. Continue staged shift.

liam: Will continue steps until eviction < 1/min or 30m have elapsed. Posting progress in this thread.

sam: Great—also update the incident doc later with exact weights/times and cost delta.
